record.title: Agent-triggered approval requests on desktop sandboxes write a screenshot PNG to the host that is never reclaimed, with no pending-approval cap
record.description: On a desktop-template sandbox, each agent tool call that policy maps to REQUIRE_APPROVAL (for example delete_file, or any exec outside the read-only allowlist) does two things. It inserts a new pending approval row, and it takes a full-screen screenshot and writes it to settings.home/captures/{approval_id}.png. Nothing counts or caps pending approvals. Nothing deletes a capture when the approval is denied, executed, failed or expired, or when the sandbox is deleted. The agent token is the lowest-trust principal, and one cheap gated call yields one retained host-side PNG. Host disk under settings.home therefore grows without bound, and the files outlive both the approvals and the sandbox. The growth is bounded only by the rate of serial docker-exec screenshots. tool_concurrency only limits concurrently running calls, and a gated call returns 202 immediately. The snapshot quota is checked only for ALLOW decisions, so it does not apply here. The container disk limit (storage_opt) is optional and off by default, and it would not cover this host-side directory in any case. The audit-row and approval-row growth is the separate v08 issue. This candidate is the capture-file retention and the missing pending cap, and it is a distinct root cause.
record.root_cause: AgentBox._call_tool writes captures/{aid}.png (service.py:325) for every REQUIRE_APPROVAL on a desktop template. No lifecycle path removes the file: expire_stale (371-382) and decide (384-422) only update approval status, SandboxManager.delete (sandbox.py:443-455) removes only the container and snapshot images, and the source contains no unlink or rmtree of captures. ApprovalStore.create (approvals.py:49-59) and _call_tool apply no per-sandbox or aggregate cap on pending approvals or on capture bytes.
record.intended_behavior: Agent-driven approval work should be bounded. A per-sandbox cap on pending approvals should reject further gated calls with 429. The request-time capture PNG should be deleted when the approval reaches a terminal state (denied, executed, failed, expired) and when the sandbox is deleted. Optionally, total capture bytes should be capped with pruning of the oldest files.

trace.description: Agent tool call (POST /sandboxes/{sid}/tools/{tool}, via call_tool). The tool name and args are chosen by the agent token holder.
default_policy.yaml returns REQUIRE_APPROVAL for delete_file and for any exec outside the read-only allowlist. Both are cheap for the agent.
When captures is configured (api.py:75) and template_of(sid).desktop is true, SandboxManager.screenshot (sandbox.py:714) returns the full PNG bytes, with no size cap.
Inserts a pending row with no per-sandbox or aggregate count check. _call_tool at service.py:321 calls it unconditionally.
Persists one PNG per approval under settings.home/captures. Nothing in service.py, approvals.py, sandbox.py or api.py removes it.

evidence.description: The only writer of captures/*.png. It runs once per REQUIRE_APPROVAL on a desktop template.
create() has no per-sandbox or aggregate pending-approval cap.
expire_stale only claims and finishes approvals as EXPIRED. It never deletes the capture file.
decide (deny, execute and failure branches) calls approvals.finish and never deletes the capture PNG.
SandboxManager.delete removes the container and snapshot images only and never touches settings.home/captures.
screenshot reads the whole desktop PNG from docker exec output with no size cap, so each retained capture can be large.
The only call-level bound is tool_concurrency (default 4). It caps in-flight calls, not total approvals or retained files, and gated calls return 202 at once.
disk_limit defaults to empty, so container storage_opt is unset by default. It would not cover the host-side captures directory anyway.

conditions.description: The attacker holds an agent token (agt_) for one sandbox. This is the lowest-trust, prompt-injection-assumed principal.
The sandbox uses a desktop template and the screenshot succeeds. The captures directory is configured by default as settings.home/captures (api.py:75).
Growth needs a sustained series of gated calls, one PNG each. The PNGs persist across approval decisions, expiry and sandbox deletion until an operator removes them.

execution.attacker_perspective: A prompt-injected agent confined to its own desktop sandbox wants to exhaust shared control-plane host disk without any human approval.
instructions: Repeatedly issue a gated tool call that default_policy.yaml maps to REQUIRE_APPROVAL. Each call returns 202 pending.
Each call creates a pending approval with no cap and writes settings.home/captures/{approval_id}.png.
Let the approvals be denied or expire, or delete the sandbox, and observe that captures/*.png remain.

Local reproduction, run inside the sbx5 wrapper: the real AgentBox._call_tool, decide and expire_stale with a real ApprovalStore, the real default policy, a stub desktop screenshot and a stub audit log.
execution.observed_result: v18 re-ran an independent copy of the harness in the sbx5 sandbox. It created 30 pending approvals with no cap, and 30 PNG files totalling 123120 bytes were written. After one deny and 29 expiries, all 30 PNGs were still on disk. A screenshot that is 4 KB in the stub would be tens to hundreds of KB on a real desktop. This harness does not show growth after sandbox deletion; that comes from reading SandboxManager.delete, which has no capture cleanup.

remediation.strategy: Bound and reclaim approval artifacts. (1) Enforce a per-sandbox pending-approval cap before creating a new approval and return 429 past the limit. (2) Delete captures/{aid}.png whenever an approval reaches a terminal state (expire_stale, decide deny, executed and failed branches), and delete all of a sandbox's captures when it is deleted. (3) Optionally cap total capture bytes and prune the oldest files.

likelihood.reason: The path needs only an agent token and cheap gated calls on a desktop sandbox. Reaching a large host-disk effect takes sustained volume at about one docker-exec screenshot per call, so it is slow and noticeable.

impact.reason: This is persistent, unreclaimed growth of host disk under settings.home that survives sandbox deletion, and an operator can recover by deleting the files. The rest of the impact is hardening: audit and approval rows (v08) and uncapped container writes grow the host disk by comparable routes, so the extra harm from this root cause is the retention and the larger per-call size.

confidence.reason: The write site, the missing cleanup and the missing cap are all in source. The independent sbx5 run reproduced 30 uncapped approvals and 30 PNGs retained after deny and expiry. The only stubbed part is the screenshot, and PNG size on a real desktop was not measured.
